cues.text: Ah. Yes. Ancient magic. The Tenth Schedule.
Not abandoned, incidentally — that's the version everyone tells. It was withdrawn. Different paperwork.
The original practitioners exceeded every understanding available to them.
They reshaped the magic of this world at will, in whatever direction pleased them, whenever they felt like, coffee not-with-standing.
Life and death. Man and beast. The inert and the living. The flow of time itself.
They went through every established boundary of the world and kept going, until they were writing magic that bent the laws of reality
and there was no schedule, no register, no form to fill in, and nobody to file it with.
One cannot tamper with what should never have existed and not be assessed for it. Proper paperwork must be filed.
The world went into absolute chaos. This was recorded as an "incident".
The survivors convened a review. I have read the findings. Four thousand pages and, in places, quite moving.
Their conclusion: the power was too great to be wielded freely by anyone.
Their second conclusion, arrived at later and with documented reluctance:
there would come a time when the power to bend the laws of nature would be necessary.
So they did not destroy it. They established sentinels - a class of authorized practitioner, licensed, reviewed, and approved.
It was clever. I want that on the record. It was genuinely clever.
The review anticipated the obvious objection. An approved practitioner is still a practitioner.
License someone and they may yet do the very thing you licensed them against.
So standing is not granted once - it is held, and reviewed, and may be withdrawn at any time by the issuing office.
And then they warded the world. Every last acre.
Not all magic, mind you. The lower nine schedules were left alone - they're the residue, and there was no appetite for the extra paperwork.
But the tenth. The ward destroys anyone who reaches above the ninth without standing.
It does not ask how they came to be without it - whether they never had it, or had it and lost it on a Tuesday.
Oh, sentinels? There are none. There has never been one. The exemption has sat unclaimed since the day the ward went up, and the post is still open.
The ward came with schedules. Schedule Two is practice without standing - that one is short, and it is thoroughly enforced.
Schedule One is implements. Every blade, every bow, every stave, every tool anyone thought worth the trouble of registering.
It is a long list. It is a good list.
But it has not been revised since the day it was written, and I have raised this. I continue to raise this.
So. If you want the tenth tier, you'll have to come and ask for it. In person. There's an application that must be completed.
I'm at the center of the world. So come when you're ready. The torches stay lit.
Bring whatever you think will help.
